authoredSolutions.31: A phenolphthalein-type dye is formed when a phenol condenses with phthalic anhydride through the ring position PARA to its \(-OH\) group. Both (A) and (R) are true, and the oxidising character described in (R) is exactly why the rubber cracks, so (R) is the correct explanation of (A). Hence the correct option is (D).
authoredSolutions.33: London (dispersion) forces arise from an instantaneous dipole inducing a dipole in a neighbouring particle. The resulting interaction energy falls off very steeply with separation, \(E \propto \dfrac{1}{r^{6}}\), i.e. \(E \propto r^{-6}\). Comparing with \(r^{x}\) gives \(x = -6\). authoredSolutions.34: Complete hydrolysis of phosphorus pentachloride gives orthophosphoric acid: \(PCl_{5}+ 4H_{2}O \rightarrow H_{3}PO_{4}+ 5HCl\). Only a hydrogen bonded directly to phosphorus is non-ionisable, and \(H_{3}PO_{4}\) has no \(P-H\) bond, so all three hydrogens are ionisable (it is tribasic). The number of non-ionisable hydrogens is therefore zero. Hence the correct option is (A).
authoredSolutions.35: The superoxide ion \(O_{2}^{-}\) has 17 electrons, giving \(\sigma_{1s}^{2}\sigma_{1s}^{*2}\sigma_{2s}^{2}\sigma_{2s}^{*2}\sigma_{2p_{z}}^{2}\pi_{2p_{x}}^{2}\pi_{2p_{y}}^{2}\pi_{2p_{x}}^{*2}\pi_{2p_{y}}^{*1}\), that is 10 bonding and 7 antibonding electrons. By contrast the cyclopentadienyl anion \((6\pi)\) and phenol \((6\pi)\) both satisfy the rule and are aromatic. Hence the keyed option is (C).
